content: Braxy is an inflammatory condition that affects the lining of the abomasum in sheep. This disease is caused by the bacterium Clostridium septicum, which is also known as Bacillus septicus. The onset of braxy is often associated with a dietary change, specifically when sheep transition from consuming succulent feed to dry or frozen (icy) feed. This condition is most commonly observed in young sheep, particularly those that have not been immunized with a vaccine targeting Clostridial infections. Sheep that are afflicted with this disease may also be referred to as braxy.
